title: Range Sum Query - Mutable
description: Design a structure over an integer array that supports point updates and inclusive range-sum queries. Implement `NumArray(int[] nums)`, `update(index, value)` to replace one element, and `sumRange(left, right)` to return the sum from index `left` through `right`. Indices are zero-based.
constraints: At most 3 * 10^4 method calls are made.
hints: Keep the original values so an update can be converted into a delta.
A Fenwick tree supports both point updates and prefix sums in O(log n).

title: Range Minimum Query with Range Updates
description: Design a structure over an integer array that supports adding a value to every element in an inclusive index range and returning the minimum value in an inclusive index range. Implement `RangeMinTree(int[] nums)`, `rangeAdd(left, right, delta)`, and `minRange(left, right)`. Indices are zero-based.
hints: A segment tree stores the minimum for each interval.
Store pending range additions as lazy values and push them to child intervals only when needed.

title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
description: For each index `i`, count values `nums[j]` that are strictly smaller than `nums[i]` for `j > i`. Return the counts in index order.
hints: Use a prefix-count structure to answer how many earlier values fall within a value range.
Coordinate compression lets a Fenwick tree store counts for only values that occur in the input.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { void add(int[] b,int i){for(;i<b.length;i+=i&-i)b[i]++;} int sum(int[] b,int i){int s=0;for(;i>0;i-=i&-i)s+=b[i];return s;} public List<Integer> countSmaller(int[] a){int[] v=a.clone();Arrays.sort(v);List<Integer> u=new ArrayList<>();for(int x:v)if(u.isEmpty()||u.get(u.size()-1)!=x)u.add(x);int[] b=new int[u.size()+1];Integer[] out=new Integer[a.length];for(int k=a.length-1;k>=0;k--){int r=Collections.binarySearch(u,a[k]);out[k]=sum(b,r);add(b,r+1);}return Arrays.asList(out);} }

title: Reverse Pairs
description: A reverse pair is a pair of indices `(i, j)` such that `i < j` and `nums[i] > 2 * nums[j]`. Return the number of reverse pairs.
hints: Use a prefix-count structure to answer how many earlier values fall within a value range.
Coordinate compression lets a Fenwick tree store counts for only values that occur in the input.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { int sum(int[] b,int i){int s=0;for(;i>0;i-=i&-i)s+=b[i];return s;}void add(int[] b,int i){for(;i<b.length;i+=i&-i)b[i]++;}int upper(int[] a,int n,long x){int l=0,r=n;while(l<r){int m=(l+r)/2;if(a[m]<=x)l=m+1;else r=m;}return l;}public int reversePairs(int[] a){int[] v=a.clone();Arrays.sort(v);int n=0;for(int x:v)if(n==0||v[n-1]!=x)v[n++]=x;int[] b=new int[n+1];int ans=0;for(int k=a.length-1;k>=0;k--){int q=upper(v,n,Math.floorDiv((long)a[k]-1,2));ans+=sum(b,q);int r=Arrays.binarySearch(v,0,n,a[k])+1;add(b,r);}return ans;} }

title: The Skyline Problem
description: Each building is `[left, right, height]` and occupies the half-open interval `[left, right)`. Return the skyline as key points `[x, height]`, where the height changes at coordinate `x`. Do not include consecutive points with the same height, and include the final point where the height returns to zero.
hints: Treat each building edge as a sweep event.
Maintain a multiset of active heights and emit a point only when the maximum changes.

title: My Calendar III
description: Implement `MyCalendarThree`. Each `book(start, end)` adds a half-open event interval `[start, end)`. After each booking, return the maximum number of events that overlap at any time.
hints: A booking adds +1 at its start and -1 at its end.
The maximum overlap is the maximum prefix sum of the ordered event deltas.

title: Falling Squares
description: Squares fall one at a time. Each `positions[i]` is `[left, sideLength]`; the square covers the half-open horizontal interval `[left, left + sideLength)`. It lands on the highest existing square it overlaps, or on the ground if none overlap. Return the maximum stack height after each square falls.
hints: Coordinate-compress every left and right endpoint into elementary horizontal segments.
Use a lazy segment tree for range maximum queries and range assignments.

title: Range Module
description: Implement a data structure that tracks a set of real-number intervals. `addRange(left,right)` adds every point in the half-open interval `[left,right)`. `queryRange(left,right)` returns true only if every point in the interval is currently tracked. `removeRange(left,right)` removes every point in that interval.
hints: Store tracked intervals as sorted, disjoint ranges.
Merge overlapping ranges on insertion and split ranges when removing an interior segment.

title: Count of Range Sum
description: Return the number of non-empty contiguous subarrays whose sum lies in the inclusive range `[lower, upper]`.
hints: Build prefix sums so each subarray sum is a difference of two prefixes.
Merge-sort the prefixes while counting right-side values that fall within [lower, upper] of each left-side prefix.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { long sort(long[] a,int l,int r,int lo,int hi){if(r-l<=1)return 0;int m=(l+r)/2;long c=sort(a,l,m,lo,hi)+sort(a,m,r,lo,hi);int i=m,j=m;for(int x=l;x<m;x++){while(i<r&&a[i]-a[x]<lo)i++;while(j<r&&a[j]-a[x]<=hi)j++;c+=j-i;}long[] t=new long[r-l];int x=l,y=m,k=0;while(x<m||y<r)t[k++]=(y==r||(x<m&&a[x]<=a[y]))?a[x++]:a[y++];System.arraycopy(t,0,a,l,t.length);return c;} public int countRangeSum(int[] a,int lo,int hi){long[] p=new long[a.length+1];for(int i=0;i<a.length;i++)p[i+1]=p[i]+a[i];return (int)sort(p,0,p.length,lo,hi);} }

title: Create Sorted Array Through Instructions
description: Insert values from `instructions` in order into an initially empty array. Before each insertion, its cost is the smaller of the number of existing values strictly less than it and the number strictly greater than it. Return the total cost modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Use a prefix-count structure to answer how many earlier values fall within a value range.
Coordinate compression lets a Fenwick tree store counts for only values that occur in the input.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { int sum(int[] b,int i){int s=0;for(;i>0;i-=i&-i)s+=b[i];return s;}void add(int[] b,int i){for(;i<b.length;i+=i&-i)b[i]++;}public int createSortedArray(int[] a){int[] b=new int[100001];long ans=0;for(int i=0;i<a.length;i++){int x=a[i],less=sum(b,x-1),greater=i-sum(b,x);ans=(ans+Math.min(less,greater))%1000000007;add(b,x);}return (int)ans;} }
